title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 19 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 19)

content.overview: Section 19 provides that the arbitral tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 or the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. Subject to Part I, parties may agree on procedure; failing agreement, the tribunal may conduct proceedings in the manner it considers appropriate, including determining admissibility, relevance, materiality and weight of evidence.

content.study:
Section 19 — Determination of rules of procedure

Section 19 provides that the arbitral tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 or the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. Subject to Part I, parties may agree on procedure; failing agreement, the tribunal may conduct proceedings in the manner it considers appropriate, including determining admissibility, relevance, materiality and weight of evidence.

Apply the provision by identifying its operative conditions, procedural stage, connected statutory provisions and precise consequence. Do not substitute generic arbitration practice for the statutory rule.
